model_selection.selected: Previously published sac_city_traffic.zip weights, copied unchanged to the dense entrypoint checkpoint.
model_selection.reason: The existing checkpoint passed all traffic tests; newly trained checkpoints had yield violations. The last candidate also triggered a separate background-vehicle contact.

map_metadata.sampling: Uniform independent passenger lanes and interior arc offsets, conditioned on connectivity and route length300..1800m.

stages.following_head: Restored unchanged from sac_city_traffic.zip before refinement.

evaluation.sampling: Uniform independent passenger lanes and interior arc offsets, conditioned on connectivity and route length300..1800m.
evaluation.selection: Evaluation routes were fixed before training and never used as optimizer samples. Validation failures led to a general randomized traffic curriculum; all original evaluation routes were retained.
evaluation.baseline_source_note: The dense baseline predates training-only curriculum changes. Evaluation defaults, physical traffic, reward and audit criteria are unchanged.
evaluation.controls: Deterministic SAC actions, without teacher throttle or runtime action replacement.
evaluation.checks: Arrival and standstill at goal, complete route coverage, all physical vehicle rectangles, lane boundaries, speed limits, signals, heading, following and crossing conflicts.

scene_regressions.controller: Published SAC steering with teacher throttle

records.fix: Recognize 0.232/m curvature on 3.5m-wide NPC routes and apply existing narrow-turn offset geometry.
Allow a committed lead to clear when the crossing vehicle is stopped before entering the conflict area.

publication.checkpoint_note: This is the previously validated local city checkpoint, published here under the dense entrypoint filename. No newer candidate replaced these weights.
publication.excluded_checkpoint: sac_dense_candidate.zip remains local because it failed yield checks.
publication.map_changes: Removed generator comments only. The complete net XML elements are byte-identical to the tested maps. Historical test-report hashes refer to the original generated files.
